questions.prompt: Did you recycle when you were a kid?

answers.basic: A little. We used to keep cardboard boxes and empty bottles separate at home. I didn't think much about why we were doing it at the time. I mostly remember folding the boxes flat so we'd have enough room to stack them by the door.

questions.prompt: Is waste sorting common in your country?

answers.basic: It's quite common where I live in Shanghai. The bins near my building have different labels, and people are used to checking them before throwing things away. For example, when I finish unpacking a delivery, I know where to take the cardboard before it piles up at home.

questions.prompt: How do you recycle things like paper and plastic?

answers.basic: I flatten boxes so they take up less space, and I empty bottles before putting them with the recyclables. I usually take them downstairs together. I keep a bag near the door for the smaller things, so I can take it with me when I go out.

questions.prompt: What do you do when you see rubbish on the street?

answers.basic: If it's something clean and easy to pick up, like a bottle, I put it in a bin. If it looks sharp or dirty, I leave it alone. There's often a bin near a subway entrance, so I can usually get rid of a bottle without going out of my way.
